newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close shade lower, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close shade lower, seen firm.

text.p: Argentine blue chips hovered in a tight band Tuesday and closed narrowly lower on selective profit-taking.
But dealers said the undertone remained firm.

"The market mirrored movements in New York -- especially U.S. Treasuries which pulled sharply back," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "But the correction here was mild and scattered, with some laggard issues like auto stocks attracting fresh buyers."
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.3 percent to 545.32, halting a four-session climb.
Traders said the outcome of the government's monthly Treasury bill auction Tuesday pleased investors.
"The interest rate fetched in the auction was very good and helped curb losses induced by Wall Street," said Alessandro.
Argentina issued $250 million in 91-day Letes at a cut-off yield of 6.1 percent, against 6.86 percent in the August auction of 182-day dollar-denominated bills.
"I think today's drop was just a technical reaction. The market is actually quite cheerful," said an analyst at a foreign-based investment bank.
He said most market players expected Congress to pass the government's five-week-old package of tax hikes when it meets Wednesday night after failing to garner quorum one week ago.
"Better late than never -- and 'never' is not even considered an option, which means the measures have been discounted by investors and priced into the market," said the analyst.
In the session floor turnover remained very slack at 13.1 million pesos compared to 15.2 million Monday. Over-the-counter volume slowed to 80.3 million pesos from 96.5 million Monday.
The broad market index closed off 0.5 percent but winners outpaced losers 23 to 14, while 25 issues closed flat.

Top main-tier performers were carmaker Sevel, which advanced 2.2 percent, power utility Central Costanera, which grew 1.5 percent, and construction stock Juan Minetti and oil company Sol Petroleo, both up 1.4 percent.
Losers were led by petrochemical concern Indupa, pulp and paper maker Celulosa and holding company Comercial del Plata, which dropped 2.8 percent, 2.6 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
